brief: Design an interface for a "Dream Architecture Studio" where users compose impossible buildings by dragging and connecting floating architectural fragments that defy physics — staircases that loop infi

dominant_strengths: Restrained typography hierarchy with crisp labels and category tags reads cleanly against the dark canvas without visual noise.
Subtle perspective grid plus colored light streaks evoke a dream-stage atmosphere that quietly reinforces the concept.
Status bar metrics (Coherence, Flux, Logic) hint at a thoughtful systemic vocabulary beyond mere decoration.
dominant_weaknesses: The 'impossible architecture' is reduced to three identical blank rounded rectangles — none of the staircases, doors, or windows are actually visualized.
No visible connection affordances, drag handles, or links between fragments, so the core compose-and-connect verb is invisible.
Right-side toolbar icons are tiny and ungrouped; canvas feels under-tooled relative to the ambition of building paradoxical spaces.
fix_priorities: Render fragments as actual stylized impossible geometries (Escher staircase, Penrose door) instead of generic cards.
Introduce explicit connection lines, ports, or magnetic snap zones so the 'compose' interaction is legible.
Add a properties/inspector panel and manipulation gizmos to give the canvas behavioral depth.
Differentiate fragment categories with stronger color coding carried into the 3D scene, not just badge pills.
rationale.norman_balance: Moody visceral atmosphere outpaces a thin behavioral layer and a reflective concept that the canvas fails to dramatize.
rationale.intent_fit: It frames the concept tastefully but doesn't actually depict impossible architecture or the act of composing it, so the brief is only half-answered.
